body:
A container declaration's reader takes the FIRST of several pointers where the door refuses more than one — and for `inboxOf`, `trust` and `posture` that reading decides a person's reach.

FOUND BY the T263 PR 2 review, in landed code, not in that PR. PR 2 closed the shape for `leeway` alone: `computeContainerTable` now refuses more than one `leeway` pointer with a named defect and reads the container as sealed, matching what `containerDefect` refuses at the door. Every other field kept the old shape.

THE SHAPE. `containerDefect` refuses a declaration carrying more than one `inboxOf` pointer (`src/gateway/container.ts`, the inboxOf clause). `computeContainerTable` reads `primitives(claims, "inboxOf")[0]`. A declaration that the door calls ambiguous therefore BINDS, taking whichever pointer its author put first, with no defect named. `trust` and `posture` have the same reading, and §28.3's pairing rule is then evaluated on that first pick — so a declaration that says `untrusted` can resolve as `curated` on shared ground.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN LEEWAY DID. `inboxOf` decides which container a pool composes into — a person's reach. `trust` decides admission. Nothing weighs a leeway yet; these are weighed today.

REACHABILITY is the same class PR 2's rails already model: not the ordinary federation path (`lawfulSnapshot` filters on `claims.author === operator`), but a restore, a replay by older tooling holding the operator key, a migration, or the §24.1 shared-seed quarantine pool.

Acceptance criteria:
- (a) THE READER AGREES WITH THE DOOR, PER FIELD: for each of `inboxOf`, `trust` and `posture`, a declaration carrying two pointers of that role resolves with the field NOT BOUND and a named defect, in BOTH pointer orders; a declaration carrying exactly one still resolves as it does today. Verify: test/gateway/container-arity.test.ts.
- (b) THE BYSTANDER SURVIVES: a sibling container declared in the same batch resolves unchanged, and the defect names only the ambiguous container. Verify: test/gateway/container-arity.test.ts.
- (c) NO REGRESSION AT THE DOOR: every declaration the door accepts today still resolves identically, proven by the existing T32 container rails staying green unchanged. Verify: `npm run check`.
- (d) THE PAIRING RULE IS NOT EVALUATED ON A GUESS: a declaration with two `trust` pointers does not resolve a posture/trust pairing at all, rather than resolving one from the first pick. Verify: test/gateway/container-arity.test.ts.
title: A container declaration's reader must refuse the arity its door refuses
